title: Quasi-compact quasi-separated derived base change from the single-complex condition
statement: In a cartesian square of schemes X' \xrightarrow{g'} X and S' \xrightarrow{g} S, with f:X\to S quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change], write f':X'\to S' for the base change of f. Let K \in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) and let L(g')^*K \to K' be a map in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'}) [def-pc-derived-category]. For x'\in X', put x=g'(x'), s'=f'(x') and s=f(x)=g(s'). Assume that for every x' and i\in\mathbf Z the canonical map H^i(K_x\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'})\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\mathcal O_{S',s'}}\mathcal O_{X',x'}\to H^i(K'_{x'}) is an isomorphism [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. Then the composite Lg^*Rf_*K \to Rf'_*L(g')^*K \to Rf'_*K' is an isomorphism in D(\mathcal O_{S'}) [def-pc-derived-base-change-map].

source.place: Tag 0DJ9 (lemma-single-complex-base-change), proof by induction principle and relative Mayer–Vietoris

proof.text: The assertion that the displayed composite is an isomorphism is local on S'. Restricting to an affine open of S' preserves the derived pullback, derived direct image, and the canonical comparison map, so it is enough to take g:S'\to S with S' and S affine; then X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the hypotheses and the cartesian square.

Let U\subseteq X be an affine open, so U=Spec(A), S=Spec(R), S'=Spec(R') and U'=U\times_S S'=Spec(A') with A'=A\otimes_R R' are affine, and the stalk hypothesis restricts to U'. Write K|_U and K'|_{U'} as \widetilde{M^\bullet} and \widetilde{N^\bullet} by the affine equivalence D(A)\simeq D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_U) [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. Since U\to S and U'\to S' are affine, hence qcqs, their derived direct images lie in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}} [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh] and correspond under the same equivalence on S and S' to M^\bullet and N^\bullet viewed over R and R' (derived global sections of a composite); derived pullback along Spec R'\to Spec R and Spec A'\to Spec A is -\otimes^L_R R' and -\otimes^L_A A' on these sheaves [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde]. Thus the base-change composite for U is the module map M^\bullet\otimes_R^L R'\to M^\bullet\otimes_A^L A'\to N^\bullet, which is an isomorphism in D(R') by the affine criterion [lem-pc-rf-single-complex-affine-base-change].

Define P(W) for a quasi-compact open W of X to mean that the analogous composite Lg^*R(W\to S)_*K|_W\to R(W'\to S')_*K'|_{W'}, with W'=(g')^{-1}(W), is an isomorphism. Step 2 gives P(W) for every affine W. By the qcqs induction principle [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology-induction], applied to the qcqs scheme X of Step 1, P(X) follows once P(U\cup V) is shown for U a quasi-compact open and V an affine open with P(U), P(V), P(U\cap V). In that situation U\cap V is quasi-compact because X is quasi-separated [pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc], and U\cup V is quasi-compact and quasi-separated over the affine S.

source.place: Tag 0DJ9, proof by the induction principle

proof.text: Apply the relative Mayer--Vietoris gluing lemma [lem-pc-rf-single-complex-relative-mayer-vietoris] to the cartesian square for f|_{U\cup V}:U\cup V\to S and its base change (U\cup V)'\to S', with K|_{U\cup V}\to K'|_{(U\cup V)'}: its hypotheses are U, V, U\cap V quasi-compact (Step 3) and the three comparison isomorphisms P(U), P(V), P(U\cap V). It gives P(U\cup V), so P holds for every quasi-compact open, in particular P(X).
